transcript.text: Let me check if the SailPoint MCP server has relevant tools for this.

This is a standard **OAuth2 client credentials grant**. Send the client ID and secret in the **POST body** (never in the URL) to your tenant's `/oauth/token` endpoint.

## Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={YOUR_CLIENT_ID}&client_secret={YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}
```

## curl example

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  --data-urlencode "client_id=${ISC_CLIENT_ID}" \
  --data-urlencode "client_secret=${ISC_CLIENT_SECRET}"
```

## Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 750,
  "scope": "..."
}
```

## Using the token

Pass it as a bearer token on every subsequent API call:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

For **beta endpoints**, also include:
```http
X-SailPoint-Experimental: true
```

## Key notes

- **Body only** — never put `client_id`/`client_secret` in the query string; ISC will reject or log it.
- **Rate limit** — 100 requests per token per 10 seconds. On a `429`, read the `Retry-After` header and wait before retrying.
- **Token lifetime** — ~750 seconds; re-exchange when it expires rather than caching indefinitely.
- **PAT cap** — each user account can hold at most 10 PATs.

---

```answer-summary
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth

required_scopes: []

```
